paper_title: Joint Detection of Fraud and Concept Drift inOnline Conversations with   LLM-Assisted Judgment
caption: A runtime comparison between our ensemble model and various LLM models on the SEconvo dataset
model_annotation: The bar chart titled “Runtime Comparison of Models in Streaming Environment” illustrates a comparison of runtimes across one “Our Joint Framework” method and several LLM models on the SEconvo dataset. The horizontal axis contains the model categories, shown left to right as: Our Joint Framework, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, LLaMA, and Claude; there is no explicit x-axis label, and the categories are not presented in alphabetical order. The vertical axis is labeled “Runtime (seconds)” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 400 with regularly spaced tick marks every 50 seconds (gridlines shown). There are five single (not grouped or stacked) vertical bars, each annotated with its exact value above the bar: “Our Joint Framework” is a dark green bar at 77 seconds; “ChatGPT” is a light blue bar at 190 seconds; “DeepSeek” is a light blue bar at 365 seconds; “LLaMA” is a light blue bar at 172 seconds; and “Claude” is a light blue bar at 243 seconds. A legend in the upper-left indicates dark green corresponds to “Our Joint Framework” and light blue corresponds to “LLM Models,” and no bars appear additionally emphasized beyond the color scheme and the numeric annotations.
